# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects — diagnostics, tool c

alls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we
use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — including in\n> breaking ways — while we
finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--st
ability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\n> [GitHub](https:/

/github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight
to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,\n> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys

page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) proje

cts — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resou
rces** — list your projects, their servers, eval\n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is\n self-serve\
n* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor** — the probe → connect → in
itialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts,
and resources** — the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and get the MCP result ba

ck verbatim
* **Read a resource** by URI
* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document
* **
Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a ful
l config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to yo
ur MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config
change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot de
tect a concurrent\n one — and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments**
— list, read, create, edit, archive, and\n restore the named execution bundles (host + optional server group + optional\n pinned
skills and plugin versions) that eval suites and goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n
* **List a project's studies** — name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link — and **read one study's settings**: model
, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable suite (name, default
model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suite
s asynchronously** — create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration result

s (tool calls, token
 usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,
 tagged `source: "api"`
* **Mana
ge a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the to

ken to a named
 account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are
 write-only: no route returns one
* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, ref
erences to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the projec
t\n* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it

; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project

in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

``

`text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this pag

e are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header

:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/
$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{}'\n`

``

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
 in the hosted app (the
card at the top of this page takes you there\n directly).\n2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization**
it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never\n stored by MCPJam in retrievable

form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound
to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a
call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never reach projects outside its organizati

on.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the

key-management surface
> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest s

essions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it fr
om an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys
narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, t
hen revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings

/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bound to an organizati

on and cannot be used — create a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Reques
ts.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads** — the catalog listings and eval-ru

n polling — are
`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope

shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ \
"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\"
: \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous
response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors ar

e opaque — don't parse them.

**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite
(the suite plus its
test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything — author once, run later. `POST /e
val-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` wit
